Japanese word of the day鏡像 · kyōzō

Kyōzō means “mirror image”: 鏡 (kagami, mirror) plus 像 (zō, image or form). In chemistry, 鏡像異性体 (kyōzō iseitai) means enantiomer—one of two molecules shaped like left and right hands. They share a formula but cannot be perfectly overlaid. Today’s Nobel story turns that visual idea into a question about why living systems chose one molecular hand. Say it as kyoh-zoh, with two even beats.
